brief.meaningEn: An action assumed to harm no one; often used in a negative claim to point out overlooked people who bear a cost.
brief.meaningZh: 被認為不會傷害任何人的行為；常用否定說法指出其實有人承擔損失。
brief.grammar: Pattern: a victimless act/crime; not a victimless act. Victimless is an adjective before the count noun; specify whose work, money or opportunity is affected.
brief.register: Measured ethical discussion: a creator or teacher tells a student why a seemingly harmless shortcut has a real affected party.
brief.boundaryZh: 要指出可辨認的受影響者與具體損失；不能單憑不喜歡某件事就斷言一定有受害者。
brief.misconceptionZh: victimless 不是指「當事人沒有抱怨」，也不表示任何行為都必然造成重大損害。
brief.outcomeZh: 能辨認看似無人受損的行為背後可能被忽略的受影響者。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 50, row 4; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Illegal copying is not a victimless act.

listening.en: A student copied a local illustrator’s poster for a paid event without asking. The organiser called it a victimless act, but the illustrator lost the fee she would normally charge.
listening.zh: 一名學生未經同意，複製本地插畫師的海報用於收費活動。主辦者說這是沒有受害者的行為，但插畫師失去了原本可收取的費用。
listening.promptZh: 為何主辦者稱它為 victimless act 不準確？

options.en: The illustrator lost a fee for work used at a paid event.
options.zh: 插畫師的作品被用於收費活動，卻失去應收的費用。

options.en: The student paid the illustrator before using the image.
options.zh: 學生使用圖片前已付費給插畫師。

options.en: The poster was drawn by the event organiser.
options.zh: 海報是活動主辦者親自繪製的。

options.en: The illustrator had agreed to offer the poster free of charge.
options.zh: 插畫師已同意免費提供海報。

listening.explanationZh: 情境明確指出插畫師失去原本可收取的費用，因此不能說完全無人受影響。

reply.promptEn: Why should the school ask before printing a photographer’s image on tickets? The photographer owns the image, usually charges for this use, and has not agreed to waive the fee.
reply.promptZh: （學校為何應先詢問攝影師，才把照片印在門票上？攝影師擁有該照片，通常會就此用途收費，而且未同意免收費用。）

options.en: The image belongs to the photographer, so permission matters.
options.zh: 照片屬於攝影師，因此應取得許可。

options.en: Using the image without paying could cost the photographer a fee.
options.zh: 未付費使用照片，可能令攝影師失去收入。

options.en: Printing it without consent is not a victimless act.
options.zh: 未經同意印製照片，並非沒有受害者的行為。

options.en: The school can ask whether the photographer would license it.
options.zh: 學校可以詢問攝影師是否願意授權使用。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都符合擁有權、收費習慣與未獲同意的情境；金句指出損失不應被忽略。

scene.promptZh: 一個商店把插畫師的作品印在商品上出售，沒有取得許可，也沒有支付原本談好的授權費。哪句最貼切？

options.en: It is not a victimless act because the illustrator loses the agreed fee.
options.zh: 這並非沒有受害者的行為，因為插畫師失去了談好的授權費。

options.en: It is victimless because the shop sold only a small number of items.
options.zh: 這沒有受害者，因為商店只賣出少量商品。

options.en: No one is affected because the illustrator did not visit the shop.
options.zh: 插畫師沒有去商店，所以沒有人受影響。

scene.explanationZh: 作品被出售而原本談好的費用未付，受影響者與損失都清楚。

contrast.promptZh: 哪一項資料最能支持「這不是 victimless act」？

options.en: The organiser says the design looks attractive.
options.zh: 主辦者說設計很好看。

options.en: The maker lost an agreed payment when others used the design.
options.zh: 別人使用設計後，創作者失去了談好的報酬。

options.en: Many people shared the image online, but no one knows its origin.
options.zh: 很多人分享圖片，但沒有人知道來源。

contrast.explanationZh: 談好的報酬未支付，能具體指出誰承受甚麼損失；吸引人或廣傳本身不足以證明傷害。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「偷偷把校刊插圖拿去賣又沒有人投訴，應該沒事吧？」你怎樣回應較貼切？

options.en: Lack of complaints does not make it a victimless act; the student artist may lose payment or control of the work.
options.zh: 沒有人投訴，不等於沒有受害者；學生畫家可能失去報酬，或無法控制作品如何被使用。

options.en: No complaint proves the student artist approved the sale.
options.zh: 沒有人投訴就證明學生畫家同意出售。

options.en: The buyer must have created the illustration.
options.zh: 買家一定是插圖的創作者。

dialogue.explanationZh: 沒有即時投訴不等於獲得同意，也不能排除創作者的損失。

speaking.en: Copying the photographer’s image for a paid poster is not a victimless act if she loses a licensing fee.
speaking.zh: 若攝影師因此失去授權費，把她的照片複製到收費海報上就並非沒有受害者的行為。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽完整示範，再指出可辨認的受影響者與損失。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：咖啡店未經同意，把一名設計師的標誌印在限量杯上出售；設計師本來會就商業使用收取費用。用一至兩句英文指出為何「沒有人受影響」的說法不成立。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出具體受影響者與可能失去的費用；不要推測未提供的其他損失。

examples.en: Using the designer’s logo on cups for sale is not a victimless act, because the designer could lose a commercial-use fee.
examples.zh: 把設計師的標誌印在杯上出售並非沒有受害者的行為，因為設計師可能失去商業使用費。

examples.en: The café should seek permission before selling the limited-edition cups; calling the unapproved use a victimless act ignores the designer’s fee.
examples.zh: 咖啡店出售限量版杯子前應取得許可；把未經批准的使用稱為沒有受害者的行為，忽略了設計師應收的費用。

takeaways.en: Before calling something a victimless act, check who may bear a real cost.
takeaways.zh: 稱某件事為沒有受害者的行為前，要先查清誰可能承受實際損失。

takeaways.en: To challenge the label victimless act, name the affected person and the specific loss.
takeaways.zh: 要質疑「沒有受害者的行為」這種說法，應指出受影響的人與具體損失。

brief.meaningEn: Seek an indirect or unofficial way around a blocked formal route, rather than use a literal entrance.
brief.meaningZh: 正式途徑受阻時，轉而尋找間接或非正規的繞路方法，而非真的找一扇門。
brief.grammar: Pattern: look/looks/looked/looking for the back door; the metaphorical object follows for. Context must establish a blocked official route and an attempted workaround.
brief.register: Informal-to-critical discussion of access: a platform manager tells a colleague why a blocked legal route may push users toward unofficial channels.
brief.boundaryZh: 只表示有人尋找繞路途徑，不等於該途徑合法、安全或已經成功。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把它理解為建築物後門，亦不要把任何正常替代方案都說成偷偷繞過規則。
brief.outcomeZh: 能在正式途徑失效的情境，辨認有人企圖尋找非正規繞路方法。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 50, row 9; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Users may look for the back door if legal access fails.

listening.en: The official archive stopped offering a legal download and gave no alternative. Some users began looking for the back door through unofficial sharing groups.
listening.zh: 官方資料庫停止提供合法下載，也沒有其他選擇。一些用戶開始透過非官方分享群組尋找繞路途徑。
listening.promptZh: 用戶 looking for the back door，意思是甚麼？

options.en: They are seeking an unofficial way around the blocked legal route.
options.zh: 他們正尋找非正式途徑，繞過受阻的合法渠道。

options.en: They are checking whether the archive building has a rear entrance.
options.zh: 他們正查看資料庫所在大樓有沒有後門。

options.en: They have found a new official download link offered by the archive.
options.zh: 他們已找到資料庫提供的新官方下載連結。

options.en: They have decided to stop looking for the material altogether.
options.zh: 他們決定完全不再尋找材料。

listening.explanationZh: 正式合法下載已停止，他們轉向非官方群組；這是尋找繞路方法，不是建築物後門。

reply.promptEn: Why are some viewers considering unofficial clips? The broadcaster removed its legal replay and has not offered another licensed way to watch.
reply.promptZh: （為何有觀眾考慮觀看非官方片段？電視台移除了合法重播，而且未提供其他獲授權的觀看途徑。）

options.en: The legal replay is no longer available.
options.zh: 合法重播已不能觀看。

options.en: They cannot find another licensed viewing option.
options.zh: 他們找不到其他獲授權的觀看方法。

options.en: Some viewers may look for the back door when the official route closes.
options.zh: 官方途徑關閉後，有些觀眾可能尋找非正規繞路方法。

options.en: The lack of an official option may push them toward unofficial clips.
options.zh: 缺少官方選項，可能令他們轉向非官方片段。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都根據合法重播被移除、沒有授權替代方案的情境；金句用「後門」比喻非正規繞路。

scene.promptZh: 線上展覽突然關閉免費入口，也未公布任何新的正式預約方法；部分人開始在私人群組交換非官方連結。哪句最貼切？

options.en: Some visitors are looking for the back door because no new official route has been published.
options.zh: 由於尚未公布新的官方途徑，部分訪客正尋找非正規方法。

options.en: The museum has clearly published a new official booking page.
options.zh: 博物館顯然已公布新的官方預約頁面。

options.en: Visitors are choosing the rear entrance of the physical museum.
options.zh: 訪客正在選擇實體博物館的後門。

scene.explanationZh: 私人群組中的非官方連結是繞過受阻正式途徑的做法；不代表它安全或適當。

contrast.promptZh: 哪種情況最不適合形容為 look for the back door？

options.en: A user tries an unapproved account-sharing group after losing authorised access.
options.zh: 失去授權後，用戶嘗試未獲批准的帳戶分享群組。

options.en: A user uses the official help page to request access through the published process.
options.zh: 用戶按公布程序，在官方協助頁申請存取權。

options.en: A seller seeks a private route around the platform’s stated booking rules.
options.zh: 賣家找私人方法繞過平台公布的預約規則。

contrast.explanationZh: 按照官方公布程序申請，不是尋找非正規繞路途徑。

dialogue.promptZh: 同事說：「合法資料庫不能登入，顧客開始問有沒有私人連結。」哪個回應最貼切？

options.en: They may look for the back door unless we restore a reliable official route; we should fix access.
options.zh: 若我們不恢復可靠的官方途徑，他們可能會尋找非正規方法；我們應修復存取問題。

options.en: A private link must be safe because customers asked for it.
options.zh: 既然顧客提出要求，私人連結就一定安全。

options.en: The login failure proves nobody needs the database anymore.
options.zh: 登入故障證明沒有人再需要資料庫。

dialogue.explanationZh: 回應指出繞路風險，並提出修復官方途徑；不替私人連結背書。

speaking.en: When the official replay vanished, some viewers started looking for the back door through private links.
speaking.zh: 官方重播消失後，有些觀眾開始透過私人連結尋找非正規途徑。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出正式途徑怎樣受阻，以及用戶轉向哪裏。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區課程的正式報名網站故障，部分人打算透過未經核實的私人群組取得名額；主辦者仍可設置臨時官方表格。用一至兩句英文描述風險和較好的處理方法。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出有人可能尋找非正規途徑，同時提出可行的官方替代；不要把私人群組說成安全。

examples.en: With the registration site down, some applicants may look for the back door through unverified groups; the organiser should offer an official temporary form.
examples.zh: 報名網站故障後，部分申請人可能透過未經核實的群組尋找非正規途徑；主辦者應提供臨時官方表格。

examples.en: Applicants are looking for the back door because the normal page has failed, so a verified replacement link would give them a safer route.
examples.zh: 一般網頁故障，申請人正尋找非正規方法；提供經核實的替代連結，會給他們更安全的途徑。

takeaways.en: Looking for the back door describes a workaround, not permission or safety.
takeaways.zh: 尋找「後門」只是在描述繞路做法，不代表獲准或安全。

takeaways.en: People may look for the back door when a reliable official route disappears.
takeaways.zh: 可靠的官方途徑消失時，人們可能尋找非正規的繞路方法。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Source is guide-written provenance; practice scenes are newly written. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: End up disadvantaged or fail to receive a benefit that someone otherwise might have gained.
brief.meaningZh: 最終處於劣勢，或失去原本可能得到的利益。
brief.grammar: Pattern: person/group lose/loses/lost/losing out; optional on + benefit or to + competitor can specify what is lost. The verb phrase is intransitive before those complements.
brief.register: Neutral everyday or economic comparison: an organiser tells a colleague which group bears the cost when a payment or opportunity is removed.
brief.boundaryZh: 要說清楚誰因此少了利益或處於劣勢；沒有拿到喜歡的東西，不一定等於在比較中吃虧。
brief.misconceptionZh: lose out 不一定是比賽輸掉，也不表示受影響者完全沒有得到任何東西。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出一項決定令哪一方失去收入、機會或相對優勢。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 50, row 14; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Independent artists lose out when payments stop.

listening.en: The streaming service changed its payment rules and paid small musicians less for the same plays. The musicians lost out while the platform kept more revenue.
listening.zh: 串流平台修改付款規則後，播放次數相同的小型音樂人卻收得更少。平台保留更多收入，音樂人因而吃虧。
listening.promptZh: 小型音樂人 lost out，是因為甚麼？

options.en: They received less money for the same number of plays.
options.zh: 同樣播放次數，他們卻收到較少款項。

options.en: They stopped making music before the rule changed.
options.zh: 規則改變前，他們已停止創作音樂。

options.en: The platform paid them more than before.
options.zh: 平台支付的款項比以前更多。

options.en: The audience listened to their songs more often.
options.zh: 聽眾比以前更常聽他們的歌曲。

listening.explanationZh: 付款規則令他們在相同播放量下收入減少，因此吃虧。

reply.promptEn: Why are independent tutors worried about the new booking fee? Every tutor must now pay it, and their earnings per lesson fall while the agency keeps the fee.
reply.promptZh: （獨立導師為何擔心新的預約費？每位導師都要支付，令每堂收入下降，而中介機構收取這筆費用。）

options.en: The fee reduces what each tutor takes home per lesson.
options.zh: 這筆費用減少了導師每堂實收的金額。

options.en: The agency keeps money that used to remain with the tutors.
options.zh: 中介機構收取了原本會留在導師手中的款項。

options.en: Independent tutors lose out under the new fee.
options.zh: 新收費令獨立導師吃虧。

options.en: Their lesson earnings fall even though they still teach the lessons.
options.zh: 即使導師照常授課，每堂收入仍下降。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都根據新預約費導致導師收入下降；金句用 lose out 概括誰因此吃虧。

scene.promptZh: 市集把小攤位的抽成提高，客流量卻沒有改變；主辦方因此收得更多，小攤主每單實收更少。哪句最貼切？

options.en: Small stallholders lose out under the higher commission.
options.zh: 抽成提高令小攤主吃虧。

options.en: Small stallholders gain more money from each unchanged sale.
options.zh: 銷售情況不變，小攤主每單賺得更多。

options.en: The organiser loses all of its commission.
options.zh: 主辦方失去所有抽成收入。

scene.explanationZh: 客流量不變但每單實收下降，吃虧的是小攤主。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不適合說小型創作者 lose out？

options.en: The platform raises its cut while paying creators less for identical sales.
options.zh: 平台提高抽成，令創作者在相同銷量下收得更少。

options.en: The platform lowers its cut and creators receive more for each sale.
options.zh: 平台降低抽成，創作者每單收得更多。

options.en: A new rule removes a payment that creators previously received.
options.zh: 新規定取消了創作者原本會收到的款項。

contrast.explanationZh: 創作者每單收入增加，沒有在這項改動中吃虧。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「新訂票制度令場地方保留更多收入，演出者每張票所得卻減少。」你怎樣回應較貼切？

options.en: Performers lose out if they receive less per ticket while the venue keeps more.
options.zh: 若場地方收得更多、演出者每張票卻分得更少，吃虧的是演出者。

options.en: Then the performers must be earning more per ticket.
options.zh: 那演出者每張票一定收得更多。

options.en: The change proves ticket sales have doubled.
options.zh: 這項改動證明票房增加了一倍。

dialogue.explanationZh: 已知分成變化足以指出誰處於劣勢；沒有資料支持收入上升或票房翻倍。

speaking.en: Small performers lose out when a new booking charge cuts their pay per ticket.
speaking.zh: 新的訂票費令小型演出者每張票分得更少，他們因此吃虧。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪一方實收減少。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：外賣平台增加向餐廳收取的每單服務費，顧客訂單量不變；小餐廳每單實收減少。用一至兩句英文比較平台與餐廳的處境。
writing.selfCheckZh: 指出餐廳在相同訂單量下實收減少，以及平台收取更高費用；正確使用本課表達。

examples.en: Small restaurants lose out because the platform charges a higher fee on each order while order numbers stay the same.
examples.zh: 訂單量不變，但平台每單收取更高費用，因此小餐廳吃虧。

examples.en: The delivery platform collects more per order, so local restaurants lose out on earnings even without a fall in customer orders.
examples.zh: 外賣平台每單收得更多，因此即使顧客訂單沒有減少，本地餐廳仍會因收入減少而吃虧。

takeaways.en: When someone loses out, name the benefit or advantage they no longer receive.
takeaways.zh: 說某人吃虧時，要指出他失去了甚麼利益或優勢。

takeaways.en: Creators lose out when a rule cuts their pay for the same work.
takeaways.zh: 規則令創作者做同樣工作卻收得更少，他們便吃虧。

notes: AI-authored provisional draft; independent English, Chinese, media and QA review remain pending. Source is guide-written provenance; practice scenes are newly written. No human or release approval is implied.

brief.meaningEn: Feels or affects someone in a distinct way because the context or listener has changed, without necessarily being stronger.
brief.meaningZh: 因情境或聆聽者的經歷改變，而帶來不同的感受；不一定較強烈。
brief.grammar: Pattern: a song, story or familiar event hits differently when/after + changed context; hit/hits/hitting are verb forms, differently is the adverb.
brief.register: Contemporary informal spoken review: one listener tells a friend how the same song feels different after a personal experience.
brief.boundaryZh: 重點是同一事物在新情境下產生不同感受；單純音量變大或品質提升，不一定適合。
brief.misconceptionZh: hit 並非實際撞擊；differently 也不自動表示更好、更差或更悲傷。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出同一作品或事件在哪個新情境下帶來不同的情緒效果。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 51, row 9; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The song hits differently when you hear it at home.

listening.en: Maya used to hear the song as a cheerful tune. After moving away from home, its lyrics about familiar streets hit differently: they now made her miss her neighbourhood.
listening.zh: Maya 以前只覺得那首歌旋律輕快。搬離家後，歌詞提到熟悉街道，帶給她不同的感受：她現在會想念舊社區。
listening.promptZh: 為何歌詞現在 hit differently？

options.en: Her move changed what the familiar streets mean to her.
options.zh: 搬家後，熟悉街道對她有了不同意義。

options.en: The singer replaced the lyrics with a new recording.
options.zh: 歌手在新錄音中換了歌詞。

options.en: The song became much louder than before.
options.zh: 這首歌的音量比以前大得多。

options.en: Maya had never heard the tune before moving.
options.zh: Maya 搬家前從未聽過那段旋律。

listening.explanationZh: 歌曲未變，變的是 Maya 搬家後的經歷與感受。

reply.promptEn: Why does the old school anthem feel different to Jonah now? He has graduated, and hearing it at a reunion reminds him of friends he no longer sees every day.
reply.promptZh: （為何舊校歌現在令 Jonah 有不同感受？他已畢業，在舊生聚會聽到校歌時，想起現在不再天天見面的朋友。）

options.en: Graduating changed what the familiar tune brings to mind.
options.zh: 畢業改變了熟悉旋律令他想起的事。

options.en: The anthem reminds him of friends he misses seeing daily.
options.zh: 校歌令他想起那些不能再天天見面的朋友。

options.en: The same anthem hits differently at the reunion.
options.zh: 同一首校歌在舊生聚會上帶來不同感受。

options.en: He now hears the tune in a setting connected with memories of school.
options.zh: 他現在是在與校園回憶有關的場合聽到旋律。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都根據畢業後在舊生聚會重聽校歌的情境；金句指出同一作品因經歷而改變感受。

scene.promptZh: 一位讀者小時候把故事中的離別當成普通情節；多年後自己搬到外地，再讀同一段時覺得特別貼身。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The passage hits differently after the reader’s move.
options.zh: 讀者搬家後，這段文字帶來不同感受。

options.en: The author secretly replaced the passage with new words.
options.zh: 作者暗中把段落改寫成新文字。

options.en: The reader now reads the passage at a higher volume.
options.zh: 讀者現在用更大聲音讀這段文字。

scene.explanationZh: 文字沒有改變；個人經歷令同一段文字的情緒效果不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情境最不適合說一首歌 hits differently？

options.en: After becoming a parent, a listener hears a familiar lullaby with new tenderness.
options.zh: 成為家長後，聽眾聽熟悉搖籃曲時感到新的溫柔。

options.en: The same recording is played through a louder speaker, but the listener’s feelings stay the same.
options.zh: 同一錄音透過更大聲的喇叭播放，聽眾感受卻沒有改變。

options.en: At a reunion, an old song brings back memories that once seemed unimportant.
options.zh: 舊生聚會上，老歌勾起從前不覺重要的回憶。

contrast.explanationZh: 音量改變而感受不變，不是本課所說的情緒效果改變。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「同一首家鄉歌，以前只覺得好聽；離開城市後再聽，卻想起很多人。」你怎樣回應較貼切？

options.en: It hits differently now that the song carries memories of people you miss.
options.zh: 如今這首歌連着你想念的人，聽來自然有不同感受。

options.en: Then the song must have changed its melody.
options.zh: 那這首歌的旋律一定改了。

options.en: A different feeling proves the song is objectively better now.
options.zh: 感受不同，證明歌曲現在客觀上更好。

dialogue.explanationZh: 新經歷改變了聽歌感受；不能因此推定旋律已改或作品客觀上更好。

speaking.en: The same childhood song hits differently after I moved away from my old neighbourhood.
speaking.zh: 搬離舊社區後，同一首童年歌曲令我有不同感受。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再說明作品未變、個人情境如何改變。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：一名學生以前把祖母的食譜當成普通紙張；學會煮那道菜後再讀，會想起與祖母一起下廚的日子。用一至兩句英文描述同一食譜帶來的新感受。
writing.selfCheckZh: 說明食譜沒有改變，但學生的經歷或回憶改變了閱讀時的感受；正確使用本課表達。

examples.en: The old recipe hits differently now that I can cook the dish and remember afternoons beside my grandmother.
examples.zh: 現在我懂得煮這道菜，又想起陪伴祖母的午後，舊食譜便帶來不同感受。

examples.en: After learning the dish, the same handwritten recipe hits differently because each line recalls our time together in the kitchen.
examples.zh: 學會這道菜後，同一張手寫食譜帶來不同感受，因為每一行都喚起我們在廚房共度的時光。

glossary.en: our time together in the kitchen
glossary.zh: 我們在廚房共度的時光

takeaways.en: A familiar song can hit differently when the listener’s life changes.
takeaways.zh: 聽眾的生活改變後，熟悉歌曲也可能帶來不同感受。

takeaways.en: A story hits differently in a new personal context; the phrase does not automatically mean better or stronger.
takeaways.zh: 故事在新的個人情境下可帶來不同感受；這個表達不自動表示更好或更強烈。
